items.title: July 2026 newsletter
items.summary:

items.title: Open letters about AI development
items.summary:
Open letters about AI development
I wrote this summary of the past few weeks of open letters as a section of my sponsors-only newsletter but I've decided to share it here as well.
Open Weights and American AI Leadership was shepherded by Microsoft, dated July 24th, and signed by 235 AI-adjacent companies including NVIDIA, Amazon, Y Combinator, The Linux Foundation and (a later signer) OpenAI.
It's clearly an argument designed to counter any instincts by the current US government to ban or limit open weight models over "safety" concerns - a reasonable consideration given what happened to Claude
items.whyItMatters: Infrastructure news is the supply side of AI: chips, memory, and hosting constraints quietly decide what tools can exist and what they cost.

brief.whoItAffects: Anyone affected by AI compute cost, speed, availability, or hardware supply.
brief.practicalImpact: Infrastructure shifts often show up later as cheaper tools, higher limits, or new bottlenecks.

items.title: 6 Questions Every Enterprise Has to Answer About AI
items.summary: Sam Altman lands in Washington into a far messier conversation than the one he planned for — hacked models, open-weights fights, and a deceleration petition — while NLW brings back six questions from the KPMG symposium that capture how completely the enterprise AI conversation has flipped from 'if' to 'how' in a single year.
